passage: As electric vehicles become more widespread, researchers are working to improve the sustainability of the batteries that power them. Traditional lithium-ion batteries rely on metals that must be mined, a process that can cause significant environmental disruption. To reduce these impacts, scientists are exploring alternative materials such as sodium, which is far more abundant and easier to extract. Sodium-based batteries currently cannot match the energy density of lithium-ion cells, meaning they store less power for their size. However, they are cheaper to produce and may be sufficient for applications that do not require long driving ranges. In addition, researchers are studying new recycling methods that recover valuable metals from used batteries, reducing the need for new mining operations. Although many of these technologies are still in early stages, they represent promising pathways toward cleaner and more sustainable energy storage.
